# Lithium industry bemoans 'paradox' of low prices, rising demand

By Ernest Scheyder

June 26, 2025 4:50 PM UTC Updated June 26, 2025

Save article Lithium industry bemoans 'paradox' of low prices, rising demand

A truck loads concentrated brine at SQM lithium mine at the Atacama salt flat, in Antofagasta region, Chile, May 3, 2023. REUTERS/Ivan Alvarado/File Photo Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab

- Supply for battery metal keeps outpacing rising demand
- Imbalance may persist until at least 2030
- Industry conference focused on cost cutting
- Lithium's future demand seen as solid

LAS VEGAS, June 26 (Reuters) - An ongoing slide in lithium prices even as demand for the battery metal continues to climb is a frustrating "paradox" not likely to be resolved before at least 2030, the world's largest producers told a major industry conference this week.
